title: Options Strategies & Breakevens

sections.heading: Core Mechanics (Rule 2360)
items: Call = right to BUY at strike; Put = right to SELL at strike.
Long = holder/buyer (pays premium, has right); Short = writer/seller (receives premium, has obligation).
American style = exercise ANY time before expiration (most equity options). European = exercise ONLY at expiration (most broad-based index options).
Settlement: equity option EXERCISE → stock delivery T+1; index options → cash settle next business day (intrinsic value).
OCC issues & guarantees all listed options; ODD must be delivered at or before account approval (Rule 2360).

items.Condition: ITM amount only; never negative; ATM/OTM = 0
Premium − Intrinsic; decays to 0 at expiration

sections.heading: Single-Leg Strategies — Max Gain / Max Loss / BE

items.Use: Income on owned stock; partial downside cushion
Insurance / hedge downside on owned stock
Same as protective put but bought same day as stock

sections.heading: Quick Formulas
items: Covered Call BE = Stock Cost − Premium received
Protective Put BE = Stock Cost + Premium paid
Straddle BEs = Strike ± (Call Premium + Put Premium)
Intrinsic (Call) = max(0, Market − Strike); Intrinsic (Put) = max(0, Strike − Market)

sections.heading: Covered vs. Uncovered (Rule 2360)
items: Covered call = writer owns the underlying (or holds long call same/lower strike & later expiry).
Covered put = writer is short the underlying or has cash secured.
Uncovered (naked) short call → UNLIMITED loss potential; highest suitability standard.
Uncovered short put → loss capped at Strike − Premium (stock to $0).

sections.heading: Suitability / Disclosure
items: ODD (Characteristics & Risks of Standardized Options) delivered at or before account approval (Rule 2360).
Options account approval & written agreement required; tiered approval by strategy complexity (Rule 2360).

common_traps: Mixing the BE rule: calls ADD premium to strike, puts SUBTRACT — students reverse them under time pressure.
Forgetting covered-call BE uses STOCK COST (not strike) minus premium; and protective-put BE uses stock cost PLUS premium (not strike).
Calling a short put 'unlimited loss' — it's limited (strike − premium); only short CALL (uncovered) is unlimited.
Confusing American vs. European: equity options = American; broad-based index options (SPX, etc.) = European/cash-settled.
Saying equity option exercise settles T+2 — it's T+1 (post-5/28/2024); index option exercise settles next business day in CASH.
Treating ATM options as having intrinsic value — intrinsic = 0 at ATM; the premium is 100% time value.
